newsitem.title: USA: Dole charges Democrats with "money laundering".
newsitem.headline: Dole charges Democrats with "money laundering".

text.p: Republican Bob Dole pledged on Thursday a get-tough battle for vote-rich California and charged Democrats with "money laundering" foreign money into their campaign.
At rallies here and earlier in Riverside, California, Dole also attacked President Bill Clinton for a "sorry record" on illegal immigration and drugs, which are heated issues in this vital state.

Dole, behind in polls but upbeat after his final debate with Clinton on Wednesday night in San Diego, told reporters he would make an "all-out" fight for the nation's most populous state's 54 electoral votes.

And following up on his earlier aggressive attacks on Clinton's White House for alleged ethical lapses, Dole told a partisan audience here in a speech that "We're going to get tough in this campaign, you haven't seen anything yet."

He accelerated his accusations that Democrats were getting thousands of dollars in what he saw as improper contributions from foreigners, a line of attack he started by criticizing earlier donations from a couple associated with the Lippo Group banking giant in Indonesia.

He told rallies the Democratic Party and Vice President Al Gore held a fund-raiser in a Buddhist temple in California, saying that although members of the sect take vows of poverty thousands of dollars were raised.
He charged that "somebody brought in the cash" and somebody passed it on.
"That's called money laundering," Dole said. "We're going to find out how much of this has been going on -- how many countries, Mr. President?
He said Democrats "are going to stonewall ... until Nov 6."

With Clinton at Universal City, California, campaign spokesman Joe Lockhart said: "Senator Dole knows full well what the election law is because he accepts the same kind of money. If he has any evidence of impropriety he should bring it forward and it will be reviewed."

As an example, Lockhart cited the Fanjuls, a Cuban-American family big in the sugar cane industry in West Palm Beach, Florida, who donate to Republicans and Democrats. Lockhart pointed out that Dole fought a proposal to cut sugar subsidies earlier this year.
Dole pledged on Thursday to "fight" for California and predicted he would win the state on Nov. 5.

His campaign manager, Scott Reed, told reporters that an overnight Dole campaign tracking poll showed Dole closing to within eight percentage points of Clinton in this state where Clinton held a lead in polls of more than 20 points last month.

Reed said the campaign would commit whatever resources were necessary to win California, the richest prize in the Nov. 5 election with its electoral votes representing about one out of every five electoral votes of the 270 needed to win election.
He later told reporters the campaign would spend "in the millions" in television ads and would start two on Friday focusing on truthfulness and trust with one featuring Dole's wife, Elizabeth.

Dole coupled his commitment to fight for California by accusing Clinton of being soft on illegal immigrants, which has been a major problem in this state that pays millions of dollars in health and education benefits to immigrants.

"Bill Clinton comes to this state with sympathetic words for the people of California," said Dole. "But the problem is this: when decision time comes, whenever he has to choose between California taxpayers and the militant groups who demand public support for illegal aliens, he sides with the special interests."

Dole said it is the federal government's responsibility to protect its borders. "During the last four years, it has failed in that duty -- big time," said Dole. "And you are the ones who pay the price for that monumental failure."
